record.field: Slow Down to Go Further: An Evening at Montgomery
How a simple breathing workshop helped our members rediscover presence, purpose, and calm

Last Thursday evening, the lights in the library room were dimmed, the noise of the city left at the door, and a circle of cushions awaited curious members ready to explore something a little outside their usual rhythm: stillness.

We welcomed mindfulness coach Leona Vervain, known for her grounded, no-nonsense approach to meditation and breathwork. With a background in neuroscience and a decade of experience leading retreats across Europe, Leona guided us through a 90-minute session called “The Art of the Pause.”

The Power of Presence

The evening began not with silence, but with laughter, as Leona shared her own struggles with slowing down in a world that celebrates speed. “I used to think productivity was my personality,” she said. “Then I burned out—and found that what I’d been avoiding all along was silence.”

What followed was a simple yet powerful practice: guided breathing, a short seated meditation, and a few gentle exercises to reconnect with the body. No incense. No awkward chants. Just presence.

“I didn’t expect to feel such a shift after only a few breaths,” said member Sophie L.

“It was like someone turned the volume down on my brain. I walked out feeling 10 pounds lighter.”

Real Conversations, Real Connection

After the session, members gathered over herbal tea and small bites in the lounge. What was striking wasn’t just how calm the room felt—it was how open everyone became. 

Conversations that began with “How did that feel for you?” quickly turned into meaningful discussions about boundaries, burnout, and balance.

“I came because I was curious. I left with a new perspective—and three great book recommendations,” said Marc T., a longtime member.

“There was something healing about seeing other people wrestle with the same things I do,” added Elena M. “It made me feel less alone.”

Slowness is a Skill

What this evening reminded us is that slowness isn’t laziness—it’s a skill. One we rarely practice, and yet deeply need. In the midst of full calendars and constant noise, it was refreshing to press pause, not just individually, but together.

Events like these are part of Montgomery’s ongoing intention to offer not just entertainment, but nourishment—for the mind, body, and spirit.

We’re grateful to Leona for holding such a safe, welcoming space—and to every member who showed up with openness and intention.

Next up: Stay tuned for our Silent Mornings pilot sessions launching in June—quiet co-working, guided journaling, and intentional starts to the day.

Because sometimes the most powerful thing you can do… is breathe.
A Hidden Retreat Tucked Within the Quiet Heart of Brussels
Where the city fades and history begins

Step through the gates of our park and something shifts. The traffic softens, the pace slows, and the trees close in around a path that leads to a place most of Brussels doesn't know exists.

Our clubhouse was never meant to be found by accident. Tucked within the green heart of the city, it sits just minutes from the busiest boulevards, yet feels like a different century altogether. The moment the doors open, gilded walls, candlelit chandeliers, and rooms that stretch on in quiet procession welcome you in, each one holding onto a little more history than the last.

This is not a place built for spectacle. It's built for the in-between moments: a coffee before a meeting, a quiet conversation with an old friend, an evening spent somewhere that asks nothing of you except to slow down. Members come here to work, to host, to think, and just as often, to do absolutely nothing at all.

What makes it different

  • A location inside one of Brussels' most treasured parks, invisible from the street
  • Interiors that carry the character of another era, without ever feeling like a museum
  • A calendar of quiet gatherings, curated dinners, and members-only evenings
  • Spaces designed for both solitude and connection, depending on what the day calls for

Brussels has no shortage of places to be seen. We built something different: a place to simply be.
Life Inside the Walls: How Our Members Shape Every Evening
A community built one evening at a time

Every great club is really just a collection of evenings, the ones people remember, the ones that turn strangers into regulars, and regulars into friends. Ours have been unfolding quietly, room by room, since the doors first opened.

On any given week, our halls might host a small dinner lit entirely by candlelight, a members' talk that runs long into the evening, or nothing more than a handful of people reading in a corner of the library. There's no fixed rhythm here, only the quiet understanding that this space belongs to whoever is using it, however they choose to use it.

What ties it all together is the setting itself. Surrounded by park on every side, the clubhouse feels sealed off from the city's usual pace. Sound softens at the door. Light moves differently through the old windows. And somehow, even a short visit tends to stretch longer than planned.

A few of the moments that define us

  • Long dinners around a single table, with no agenda but good company
  • Evening talks and small salons hosted by members, for members
  • Afternoons spent alone with a book, a coffee, and a view of the park
  • Seasonal gatherings that mark the turning of the year together

We don't measure the club by its rooms, its chandeliers, or its address, though we're proud of all three. We measure it by the evenings its members choose to spend here, again and again.
